questions.q: What is the shared core schema's architectural role in a federated governance system?
options: It defines the common tags and fields every domain catalog must populate for cross-cutting data, making shared standards checkable
It replaces the need for any domain-owned catalog
It is only used for internal IT billing purposes
It has no architectural function — it's purely a legal document
questions.explain: The shared core schema is the concrete artifact that turns 'shared standards' from an aspiration into something checkable.

questions.q: What does the central index (catalog-of-catalogs) hold in a federated architecture, per this lesson?
options: Registrations of which domain catalog owns which data, plus the shared-schema fields — not full local detail
The complete detailed metadata for every table in every domain
Nothing — federated architectures have no central index
Only financial data, excluding all other categories
questions.explain: The central index is deliberately lightweight: it registers ownership and exposes shared fields, not full domain detail.

questions.q: What is the 'two-tier policy split' in federated architecture?
options: Global policies enforced the same way everywhere, paired with local policies a domain controls itself
Two completely separate, unrelated sets of central policy with no domain input
A split between paid and unpaid governance staff
A policy that only applies on alternating weeks
questions.explain: The two-tier split separates centrally-enforced global policy from locally-controlled domain policy.

questions.q: What real, documented example does this lesson give of connectors pulling metadata into a central system while data stays with its source?
options: Microsoft Purview's connector model
A fictional product invented for this lesson
A product with no public documentation of any kind
A spreadsheet macro
questions.explain: The lesson cites Microsoft Purview's documented connector/scanning model as a real example of this federated integration pattern.

questions.q: Per this lesson, where does federated architecture's real complexity actually live?
options: In actively maintaining the shared schema's boundary between centrally-governed and locally-governed data
In the physical cost of server hardware
In the number of employees a company has
Federated architecture has no meaningful complexity at all
questions.explain: The lesson states the real complexity is maintaining the shared-schema boundary — too thin loses consistency, too thick loses local autonomy.
